title: Preamble — constitutional values (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: the Preamble expresses sovereign democratic republic ideals and goals including justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity. Courts sometimes use it interpretively, but operative provisions are found in the articles that follow.

title: Fundamental Rights (Part III) — overview (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: Part III guarantees enforceable rights (e.g. equality before law, freedoms of speech and association, protection of life and personal liberty, remedies via writ jurisdiction). Reasonable restrictions appear in several clauses.

title: Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV) (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: Part IV sets non-justiciable goals guiding governance (education, health, environment, workers’ interests). Courts may harmonise statutes with these principles where possible without violating fundamental rights.

title: Basic structure doctrine (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: judicial doctrine holds Parliament cannot amend away certain foundational features (e.g. democracy, rule of law, judicial review). Exact contours evolve through Supreme Court decisions—always check current holdings.
